title: Runoff at equal rain stayed high during and after the WWII drought but fell after the Millennium Drought at 24 south-east Australian gauges; earlier 13-year deficits were similar (SILO, 1889-2025)
abstract:
Question: campaign work found that after 1997 south-east Australian (SE-AU) runoff fell about 15-25% below each catchment's 1951-1996 rainfall-runoff relation and stayed low. All of it starts in 1950. Did the World War II drought (1937-1945), with an equal rain deficit, also leave a runoff deficit, and is the post-1997 deficit larger than earlier decade-scale departures?

Approach: 58 CAMELS-AUS gauges with Bureau of Meteorology daily flow records from 1885-1950 to 2025; SILO rain from 1889 averaged over catchment boundaries, checked against a fixed network of 54 long-record stations (ratio 0.984-0.996 in all periods). Annual model Q = a + bP + cP(t-1); 2-degree cell bootstrap. Plan and a paired-test addendum were written before results.

Results: at the same 24 SE-AU gauges and the same 1957-1996 relation, runoff was +23.7% (95% CI +11.4 to +42.3; n=11) during the WWII drought and +32.0% (+5.6 to +46.3) in 1946-1955, but -6.9% (-15.6 to 0.0) in 1997-2009 and -12.0% (-22.1 to -8.0) in 2010-2025. Rain deficits were -17% and -18%. The post-drought difference was -44 points (-58 to -21); 22 of 24 gauges were lower. At matched rain the result was the same. It held without regulated gauges, with station rain and with a quadratic term. Before 1957, 17 of 18 SE-AU gauges had more runoff than the 1957-1996 relation (median +19%) at equal rain. Post hoc, cross-validated 13-year departures before 1997 ranged from -12.7% to +25.8% (group mean); post-1997 windows were -9% to -14%, equal to the 1959-1971 and 1983-1995 lows. Only 4 of 17 gauges had a 2010-2022 window below all their earlier windows. Northern control gauges had a 20-33% deficit in the 1980s-1990s and recovered after 2009.

Conclusion: a long drought did not leave a deficit in 1937-1955; runoff efficiency varies at multi-decadal scale, and the 1951-1996 reference includes the end of a high period. The post-1997 SE-AU deficit is at the low edge of earlier variation, not clearly beyond it.

Limitations: few early gauges (4-11 for pre-1937 or WWII windows); possible early rating errors; land-use change after 1945 not separated; several results are post hoc; causes not tested.
